chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both together, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Salamah, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khadijah, who said:

I entered upon Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, and he said to me: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has strengthened the believer with a spirit from Him. It is present with him at every time in which he does good and is Godwary, and it is absent from him at every time in which he sins and transgresses. So it is with him, trembling with joy at his doing good, and sinking into the earth at his doing evil."

So take care, O servants of Allah, of His blessings by rectifying yourselves; you will increase in certainty and gain a precious and valuable profit. May Allah have mercy on a man who intended good and then did it, or intended evil and then refrained from it.
Then he said: "We strengthen the spirit through obedience to Allah and working for Him."

key_terms.اَلْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer who is divinely strengthened
key_terms.بِرُوحٍ: with a spirit by which the believer is supported
key_terms.يَتَّقِي: he is Godwary and guards himself from sin
key_terms.يَقِينًا: certainty and firm conviction in faith

ai.seo_question: How does Allah support the believer according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer is supported by a divine spirit that accompanies him in moments of obedience and taqwa, but withdraws at times of sin and transgression. It exhorts believers to preserve Allah’s blessings through self-rectification, increase in certainty, and restrain themselves from evil while acting upon good.
